title: Waypoint (the unit of human derivation)
description: A derivation writes waypoints, not minutes. A waypoint states: at about t (window lo..hi, LMT) the unit was at pos (+- sigma_m), facing, in formation, doing activity, on the authority of the cited sources and one verbatim quote that tools/check_quotes.py finds in the source text. The per-minute rows are generated from the waypoints by tools/pilot_lib.py. Relative waypoints (rel) hang on an earlier waypoint of the same unit: this is how the Confederate advance chains off one step-off time.

rel.description: [ref_wid, dt_best_min, dt_lo_min, dt_hi_min]; exactly one of t/lo/hi or rel

sigma_m.description: about a 95 percent half-width of the position claim; 40 m for a monument, 150 m and more for a position read from prose

quote.description: verbatim from a source in srcs (OCR errors preserved; check_quotes.py folds case, punctuation and line breaks)
